key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (>5% and more frequent than placebo): arthralgia, injection site erythema, injection site pruritis, pain in extremity, peripheral edema, and myalgia. Key warnings include elevated IGF-I (47.4% with IGF-I SDS >2 at 26 weeks), glucose intolerance/diabetes, fluid retention, and injection site reactions (24.5% vs 14.4% placebo).

citations.quote: Most commonly reported adverse reactions (>5% and more frequent than placebo): Arthralgia, injection site erythema, injection site pruritis, pain in extremity, peripheral edema, and myalgia. (6.1)

Among patients who received EGRIFTATM for 26 weeks, 47.4% had IGF-I levels greater than 2 standard deviation scores (SDS), and 35.6% had SDS >3, with this effect seen as early as 13 weeks of treatment.
The incidence of injection site reactions was 24.5% in EGRIFTATM-treated patients and 14.4% in placebo-treated patients during the first 26 weeks of treatment in the Phase 3 clinical trials.
• Fluid retention: May include edema, arthralgia, and carpal tunnel syndrome. (5.3)
• Glucose intolerance: May develop with EGRIFTATM use. Evaluate glucose status prior to and during therapy with EGRIFTATM. (5.4)
